correctness.rationale: Exact pair-scatter identity gives n(n-1)S; cyclicity of trace yields n(n-1)p whenever every pair is active and S is positive definite. The explicit six-row, two-dimensional example has six missing variables, full-column-rank frozen-covariance design, SPD initial covariance and two distinct SPD completions, each attaining the same constant objective. Spectral decomposition proves the ridge identity, and binomial counting/Poisson limit/variance control rigorously give the MCAR regimes. A standalone program replayed the deterministic checks and numerical mask probabilities; finite checks supplement the proof rather than substituting for it.

originality.rationale: The all-pair sample-covariance trace identity is standard rather than independently novel, but the original 2026 article does not apply it to its active-pair, covariance-updating imputation objective. Its rank theorem concerns the frozen-covariance linear stage. A full-rank witness demonstrates that stage is no protection against completely flat nonlinear refinement. The exact MCAR logarithmic mask threshold is a consequential source-specific derivation. The closest independent imputation predecessor establishes Mahalanobis depth/iterated-regression links, not constant active-pair sums with recomputed sample covariance. Source-specific and synonym searches, the public findings index, and historical claim overlap comparison found no decisive covering prior statement; this is not a claim of absolute uniqueness.
residual_risks: A recent, unindexed preprint may mention the same collapse; failure to locate it is not a proof of novelty.
Different covariance normalizations rescale the flat constant, so the quantitative identity relies on the cited sample-covariance divisor n-1.
The result does not imply that all possible observed missingness masks are flat or that a ridge-updated criterion is flat.
The source could have used undocumented implementation safeguards; no assertion about unavailable code is made.

value.rationale: The paper motivates nonlinear covariance updating as a refinement of missing-value imputation, and its rank theorem supports only the frozen-covariance step. Identifying complete loss of its nonlinear objective even with an invertible, full-rank linear formulation exposes a genuine objective-function identifiability boundary, not a low-impact arithmetic slip. The exact independent-cell MCAR threshold makes the obstruction operationally useful in high-dimensional design; it sharply delineates when changing the target or introducing independent information is necessary, without extrapolating to source experiments.
